## 1. Learning objectives
After this lesson you can:
- write an **enum** (a fixed list of named values) and explain why it is safer than a `String`;
- give an enum fields and methods, loop over `values()`, and use `valueOf`;
- write a **`switch` expression** that the compiler checks is complete;
- write a **record** and explain what Java generates for you;
- say when a record fits (plain data, never changes) and when a normal class fits (behaviour, changing state).

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- In lesson 13 a staff member's role was a `String`: `"cashier"`. Typing `"cahsier"` compiles, runs and quietly
  gives the wrong answer. An **enum** is a type with a **fixed list of possible values**: `Role.CASHIER`,
  `Role.MANAGER`. Nothing else can be a `Role`, and the compiler catches typos.
- Enum constants are written in `UPPER_CASE`. An enum may have fields, a constructor, and methods, because each
  constant is an object: `PaymentMethod.GCASH.label()` is `"GCash"`. Helpful built-ins: `values()` (all constants, in order),
  `valueOf("CASH")` (find by exact name), `name()`, `ordinal()` (position, from 0).
- A **`switch` expression** (`return switch (this) { case RECEIVED -> quantity; case SOLD -> -quantity; };`) produces a
  value. With an enum the compiler complains if you forget a constant. Add a new constant later and every incomplete
  `switch` stops compiling: bugs found before the program runs.
- A **record** is a short way to write a class that is just data. `record StockMovement(String productName,
  MovementType type, int quantity) { }` makes the private final fields, the constructor, the accessors (`productName()`,
  with no `get`), `equals`, `hashCode` and `toString`. A record **never changes** after creation.
- **Value equality.** Two records with the same values are `equals`, even though they are different objects.
  Two `SaleLine("Salt", 3500, 2)` are equal. (With normal classes, `equals` needs to be written by hand.)
- **The stock log.** Every accepted `receive` and every sale adds a `StockMovement` (`RECEIVED` or `SOLD`) to a list in the
  `Inventory`. Because every product starts at 0, "received minus sold" must equal what is on the shelf:
  `netMovement(name) == quantityOf(name)`. A bookkeeper calls this an audit trail.
- **Intentional refactors in this lesson:**
  1. `Staff`'s role changes from `String` to the `Role` enum. Constructor calls and tests change from `"cashier"` to `Role.CASHIER`.
  2. `SaleLine` changes from a class with getters to a **record**. `line.getProductName()` becomes `line.productName()`; every
     use in `Sale`, `Inventory` and the tests is updated. Behaviour is the same.
  3. `Sale` gets a `PaymentMethod` (default `CASH`), and `Inventory.sell` gets a five-argument overload that takes it.
- **Honest limits.** The log only sees changes made through `Inventory`. Anyone holding a `Product` from `products()`
  could still call `product.receive(5)` directly and bypass it; closing that is a design question for the database weeks.
  The menu does not ask for a payment method yet (the `Sale` records `CASH`).

```

enum Level { LOW, OK, HIGH }                       // a fixed list of names
record Point(int x, int y) { }                      // a data class in one line
```

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `the switch expression does not cover all possible input values` | A constant is missing from the `switch` | Add the missing `case`, or you added a new constant and have not handled it yet |
| `cannot find symbol: method getProductName()` | `SaleLine` is a record now | Use `productName()` |
| `cannot assign a value to final variable` on a record field | Records never change | Make a new record with the new value (`moved(...)`) |
| `NullPointerException` from `PaymentMethod.fromText(...)` result | The text matched no constant and the method returns `null` | Check for `null` before using it |
| `IllegalArgumentException: No enum constant ...` | `valueOf("gcash")`: the name must match exactly, capitals included | Use `valueOf("GCASH")`, or `fromText` for friendly text |
| Two equal-looking records are `!=` | `==` compares objects, not values | Use `.equals(...)` |
| `netMovement` is different from the shelf | A change was logged twice or not at all | Log exactly once, only after the product accepted the change |
